How To Apply For Graduate Studies In Geosciences At Penn State
How to Apply for Graduate Studies in Geosciences at Penn State
Thank you for your interest in applying for graduate study in the Department of Geosciences at Penn State. The department offers a vigorous graduate education with some of the top researchers in the nation. Dedicated to academic and professional excellence, our faculty members emphasize both fundamental and interdisciplinary study. Our faculty have high research productivity and are committed to education and to cultivating individual skill development for each graduate student in our program. Thank you for considering us for your graduate education.
Deciding to apply to graduate school is a big deal! You may not know anyone who has done it before or feel like you don't know what to do.
Before applying, check out the resources below designed to help you throughout the application process. Please don’t hesitate to reach out and contact us with any questions.
After reviewing the resources below, please visit the Graduate School at Penn State to apply for graduate studies in the Department of Geosciences.
Visit Graduate School to Apply
Resources for applying
View the resources below to designed to help you with the application process.
Eligibility
Students are expected to have a bachelor's degree in some branch of the natural or physical sciences, engineering, or mathematics by the start of their graduate program. A student also is expected to have completed standard introductory courses in geosciences, chemistry, physics, and mathematics through integral calculus, plus an equivalent of 15 credits of intermediate-level work in one or a combination of these subjects.
Students who are admitted but have less than the minimum preparation in these subjects may be asked to address their deficiencies prior to entry to the program. They may take courses concurrently with their graduate studies, but this is not encouraged. Students with special backgrounds, abilities, and interests whose undergraduate grade-point average in courses pertinent to geosciences is below a 3.00 (on a 4.00 scale) will be considered for admission only when there are strong indications that a 3.00 average can be maintained at the graduate level.
Students are admitted either to the M.S. or Ph.D. degree program. A student may work toward a Ph.D. degree without first earning a M.S. degree.
For more information about Penn State Graduate School requirements, please visit the Requirements for Graduate Admission webpage.
Application Requirements
The Department of Geosciences graduate application is available through the Penn State Graduate School. The application includes:
Online form to provide personal, contact, and other applicant information, including a list of prospective graduate advisers
Course summary to provide information on academic preparation (this is a department-specific requirement that must be uploaded to the Graduate School application portal)
Official transcripts for all undergraduate college and universities
Response to five prompts (see below)
Contact information for three reference letters
Fee of $65
The GRE is not required.
The Penn State application does not require a single personal statement or statement of purpose but rather five short responses to prompts (250 words maximum per response) in which applicants can describe their;
Problem-solving abilities
Fesilience and adaptability
Motivation and future goals
Respect for diversity and inclusion,
Additional relevant experiences and self-awareness
Our application utilizes these prompts to provide a holistic picture of applicants and to highlight aspects of applicants’ experiences and background that are not always included within the traditional single statement.
Admissions and application process
The deadline to apply to start a graduate program in the fall semester is December 15 of the preceding year. Please note that applications will still be considered after December 15, although the selection process and considerations for support generally begin at the end of calendar year. Decisions will be made in the spring through an Admissions Committee.
Timeline:
December 15
Applications due to the Graduate School
Late December – Early January
Geosciences Admissions Committee begins review of applications
Late January-February
Acceptance letters sent
February-March
Campus visits scheduled
April 1
Deadline to accept a graduate student offer
Adviser/Research Mentor
Identifying a research mentor, or adviser, is a critical step in the graduate application process. Please read about our different research focus areas and explore the faculty in our department. Students are often co-advised by more than one faculty supervisor, and graduate committees and seminars and reading groups provide rich intellectual exchanges and community support for research and inquiry in disciplinary areas and across the Geosciences Department as a whole.
Fellowships and funding
While all accepted graduate students are guaranteed funding for their stipend and tuition, which can come from a combination of different sources, support that is tied to a specific research grant generally means that the graduate student under that grant will work on a research project closely related to the proposed work. Therefore, obtaining external funding can be highly desired because it provides students with the freedom to determine their own project regardless of the projects that are funded by their graduate adviser. We encourage all applicants to consider applying for external fellowships and to discuss the possibility of these opportunities to their prospective Penn State adviser, such as the ones listed below (please confirm your eligibility):
National Science Foundation Graduate Research Fellowship
Department of Defense National Defense Science and Engineering Graduate Fellowship
Future Investigators in NASA Earth and Space Science and Technology (FINESST) Fellowship
Ford Foundation Fellowship
International Students
TOEFL Code: 2660 (Institution Code)
As part of the online application process, you are required to upload electronic copies of transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended (or equivalent documents for institutions outside the U.S., e.g. degree/study certificates, diplomas, etc.) in the language of instruction, as well as copies of an official English translation, if English is not the language of instruction. (If you are offered admission, Penn State's Graduate School will request official transcripts by postal mail. Note: Offers of admission will be revoked if original, official documents do not arrive by specified deadlines, or if official documents do not match electronic copies provided prior to the offer of admission.
You will also be required to provide official TOEFL scores to Penn State. You do not need to send a copy by mail if official scores are reported electronically in this manner. TOEFL or IELTS scores, can be submitted electronically to Penn State by the administering agency. All international applicants whose first language is not English or who have not received baccalaureate or master's degrees from an institution based in the U.S. or other countries (see full list here ), must take the TOEFL (Test of English as a Foreign Language) examination. A TOEFL score of 550 on the paper test is required for admission. If you take the iBT (internet-based TOEFL test), the minimums are 80 (total score) and 19 (speaking). Please contact the Graduate School for more information about language requirements and other information relevant for international students.
Note that your application will not be considered complete until you have filed your online application AND we have received the TOEFL (if required), by official electronic submission to Penn State from the administering agency.
